title: 영어브리핑_2026-10-31
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 08:00 전 SO 0018 트럭·항공편 확인, 08:30 원단·실 실사 브리핑, 실사 후 COATS 원사 미신고 법인장 직접 보고. Chamin 회신·보안서약 완료보고도 오늘.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Saturday, October thirty-first. This is your last workday of the week, and it is a big one.
The fabric and thread count starts at eight thirty. Mr Chamin also has his last day today. And rain is still expected until November fourth.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is the reports to collect. Part three is the replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is English review. Part six is a role-play. Part seven is a short recap of your first actions. Part eight is the closing.
Let's start.
Part one. Top three for today.
Number one is the physical count of fabric and thread. You sent the final plan yesterday with a high importance flag. The team will check random lines from the QR system against the real stock.
Why does it matter? The QR system is only useful if its numbers match the real rolls. This count will show how much we can trust it. It will also show the gap against the customs data.
Your first action is simple. Be at the warehouse at eight thirty for a ten minute briefing. Check that Mint printed the sheets, and that each person has a sheet with their name.
Also check that cutting is not taking fabric. You asked Mint to tell Myna that no fabric leaves the warehouse until eleven ten. One roll moving during the count can make the result wrong.

Number two is the truck for the Vince air shipment. The shipping order ends in zero zero one eight. The truck was planned for eight o'clock this morning. The first plan was a flight on November first.

But yesterday, Hecny sent new information. A typhoon hit Taipei last week, and all the air hubs are now crowded. Korean Air can only offer a flight on November third, with a cut-off on November second. Hecny is still waiting for the agent and the consignee to confirm.

Why does it matter? If the truck goes today, the boxes may wait at the airport. If the truck is not moved, nobody may have told the driver. The planned delivery date has also passed, so the buyer may ask questions.

Your first action is to ask Ms Trinh Do before eight o'clock. Ask if the truck is still going, and if the booking is confirmed. You could say, "Has the truck been rescheduled, and have we received the booking confirmation?"

Number three is the COATS thread with no customs record. This is now one week old. You asked Ms Trinh Do for a table by invoice, receipt date, quantity and current stock. I could not find that table in your email.
Why does it matter? Today's count can show this thread as a gap between QR and customs. Mr Moon should hear about it from you first, not from a number on a sheet.

Your first action is to ask for the table this morning, after the count starts. Then give Mr Moon a short report today, even if the table is not complete. Tell him what you know, and what is still open.
Part two. Reports to collect.
First, Mint. Yesterday you asked her to assign racks for the forty-five fabric lines with no location in QR. You asked her to tell you when it was done. I found no reply from her yesterday.
Check this in the QR system before the briefing. Then you can say, "Please confirm that the forty-five fabric lines now have a rack location."
Second, Ms Trinh Do and Thu Hien. They must find seventeen styles on the export and import sheet by ten o'clock. They write found or not found, the location, and the number of rolls.
At ten o'clock, you can say, "Could you confirm whether all seventeen styles were found?"
Third, Ms Trinh Tran and Ms Nga. They check sheet C with Mint, which has twenty locations. At ten forty, they count five lines each from sheets A and B again. This second count tests the first count.
You can say, "Please let me know if you find any discrepancy between the two counts."

Fourth, Mai in purchasing. Yesterday's morning check had three late items. They are Mr Asanka's e-ticket, the consumables ledger, and the quotes for the thirty-nine relaxing racks. I found no email from Mai since Thursday morning. She may have replied by another way, so please check Zalo first.
Mr Asanka now arrives on November tenth, so the ticket matters most. You can say, "Mai, please send the e-ticket first, then tell me when I will get the other two."

Fifth, Ms Trinh Do has two more items due today. One is the Ex-Im Ledger for September, with her two answers. The other is the logistics cost report for January to June. Head office has already reminded us three times about that report.
You can say, "Just a reminder that the ledger and the logistics report are due today."

Sixth, Ms An. You asked her yesterday for the test result of the new roller cleaner, SEVICH. The first date was October twenty-eighth, and you gave her until this morning. S O P reported that the fusing machine stained fabric again, so this is urgent.

There is also a small conflict. Ms An says the purchase request is not approved. Van says it was approved on October twenty-ninth, and she will add it to the list next week. You can say, "Van says the request was approved. Please check with her and tell me the new test date."

Seventh, Ms Trinh Tran. The roof repair company was due yesterday at eight o'clock. You asked for the repair locations and photos from before and after. I found no reply yesterday. You can say, "If the roof repair was rescheduled, please tell me the new date."

Eighth, Ms Ly. She should enter the October working hours in the system today. Head office needs them by eleven o'clock on Monday. Review her entry before you leave. You can say, "Please tell me as soon as the working hours are entered."
Part three. Replies you owe.

The first reply is to Mr Moon, about the COATS thread. He has not received a direction from you yet. A good first sentence is, "Mr Moon, I'd like to highlight one customs issue that today's count may show."

The second reply is to Mr Richard Lee at head office. The local staff completion report for the security pledge was due yesterday. I did not see it in your sent email. Please check how many signed forms came back, then send it today.
A good first sentence is, "I'm following up on the security pledge report that was due on October thirtieth." Add the names of anyone who has not signed yet.
The third reply is to Mr Chamin. He asked about his return flight and his baggage. He also mentioned the leave he did not take in September. I did not see your reply in yesterday's sent email.

Today is his last day, so please answer today. A good first sentence is, "Please note that I will check the ticket rule and reply by Monday." Only say this if it is true. If you already know the rule, simply give it.

The fourth reply is to Mr Quan. He asked before how to collect the laptop from Mr Chamin, because he is not coming to work. Today is the date Mr Quan said he would remind you. If you have not answered yet, connect this with your message to Mr Chamin. Ask when he can return the laptop, the adapter, the mouse, and the room key.
The fifth reply is to Ms Ly, about the leave forms for Line One. She left the original forms on your desk. Please compare them with her list when you have ten quiet minutes.
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.
There are no meetings in your Outlook calendar today. Here is your own plan.

At eight thirty, the warehouse briefing. At nine, you check the weekly report from the C M P team. At nine forty, you review the short-term contract payroll. At ten, the seventeen styles are due. At ten forty, the second count. At eleven ten, the warehouse opens for cutting again.

Today is also the last day of your checks for several open items. These are the CAD room report, the broken pallet photos, and the sponging machine water drops. The QR warehouse work also has today as its target.
The party room has its first booking at lunch today. Ms Diem checks the cleaning. There is no key for that room yet, so please make sure the room is open. Your weekly English test is also today.
Sunday is your day off. On Monday, November second, you have the wood fuel report and the working hours deadline at eleven. New electricity and water bills also arrive.

Monday is also the first working day after two monthly tasks. They are the Korean staff leave report and the CEO's organization chart review. On Wednesday, November fourth, Ms Tho finishes the party room lock and QR poster.
One small correction. Your email to Ms Thao in I E says, "November fourth, Tuesday." But November fourth is a Wednesday. If you meet her, please tell her which day you mean.
Part five. English review. Listen, then say each sentence with me.
The expression is proceed. It means to go ahead with a plan. For example, please proceed with the Malaysia Airlines option. Now say it with me.
Please proceed with the Malaysia Airlines option.
One more time. Please proceed with the Malaysia Airlines option.
The expression is reschedule. It means to set a new date or time. For example, if the roof repair is rescheduled, please tell me the new date. Now say it with me.
If the roof repair is rescheduled, please tell me the new date.
One more time. If the roof repair is rescheduled, please tell me the new date.
The expression is in case. It means if this thing happens. For example, in case the power goes out, please start the generator. Now say it with me.
In case the power goes out, please start the generator.
One more time. In case the power goes out, please start the generator.
The expression is please note that. It helps you give important information politely. For example, please note that the ticket includes only twenty-five kilos of checked baggage. Now say it with me.
Please note that the ticket includes only twenty-five kilos of checked baggage.
One more time. Please note that the ticket includes only twenty-five kilos of checked baggage.

The expression is discrepancy. It means a difference between two numbers or records. It is a good word for today. For example, could you explain the discrepancy between the two counts? Now say it with me.
Could you explain the discrepancy between the two counts?
One more time. Could you explain the discrepancy between the two counts?
The expression is please keep me posted. It means please keep telling me the latest news. For example, please keep me posted on the flight until it is confirmed. Now say it with me.
Please keep me posted on the flight until it is confirmed.
One more time. Please keep me posted on the flight until it is confirmed.
The expression is hold off on. It means to wait and not do something yet. For example, please hold off on the truck until the booking is confirmed. Now say it with me.
Please hold off on the truck until the booking is confirmed.
One more time. Please hold off on the truck until the booking is confirmed.
The expression is log. It means to write down a result or a number. You missed this one on the last test. For example, please log the count result on the sheet. Now say it with me.
Please log the count result on the sheet.
One more time. Please log the count result on the sheet.
The expression is comply with. It means to follow a rule or a standard. You also missed this one. For example, the new cleaner must comply with the buyer's rules. Now say it with me.
The new cleaner must comply with the buyer's rules.
One more time. The new cleaner must comply with the buyer's rules.
Part six. Role-play. It is after the count. You are reporting to Mr Moon. I will read both voices.
Anthony says, "Mr Moon, do you have five minutes? I'd like to update you on today's count."
Mr Moon says, "Yes, go ahead. How did it go?"
Anthony says, "We finished the count this morning. I will send you the numbers after we check the sheets."
Mr Moon says, "Did you find any big problems?"
Anthony says, "I'd like to highlight one point. The COATS thread is in the factory, but it has no customs record."
Mr Moon says, "Why is there no record?"
Anthony says, "The supplier delivered directly to our factory, and the invoice buyer is our head office. So it never went through our customs records."
Mr Moon says, "How much thread is it?"
Anthony says, "I'm still waiting for the final table. I asked for the invoices, quantity and current stock. I will send it as soon as I have it."
Mr Moon says, "All right. Is there anything else?"
Anthony says, "Yes. The Vince air shipment is delayed. All the air hubs are crowded, and the earliest flight may be November third."
Mr Moon says, "Does the buyer know?"
Anthony says, "Hecny has asked the agent and the consignee to confirm. I will keep you posted."
Mr Moon says, "Good. Thank you."
Now say the two key sentences with me.
I'd like to highlight one point.
I'd like to highlight one point.
I will send it as soon as I have it.
I will send it as soon as I have it.
Part seven. Your first actions, once more.
Before eight o'clock, ask Ms Trinh Do about the truck and the booking. Before eight thirty, check the forty-five lines in QR. At eight thirty, start the count briefing.
Part eight. Closing.
If you do only one thing today, finish the count and report the COATS thread to Mr Moon yourself.
Good luck today. Enjoy your Sunday, and see you on Monday.
